newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mixed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends volatile session mixed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in choppy dealings on Friday, as a last-minute combination of trade buying and local short-covering lifted prices off lows, dealers said.
"The market came back strongly in the last 16 minutes," one dealer said. "The trade caught the locals short."

Speculative profit taking and steady pressure on the March/May switch drove the March contract down more than 3.00 cents a lb to a low of 137.00 cents before the market bounced back. By the close, March delivery stood at 139.40 cents, down 0.90 cent on the day.
Second-position May finished up 0.45 cent, to 134.95 cents, while the outer months closed 0.20 to 1.05 cent higher.
Despite two consecutive sessions of losses, the March contract gained 2.50 cents on the week as speculators bought heavily on supply concerns.
Traders await the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report, which most market participants expect to show an increase in speculative (non-commercial and nonreportable) long positions.

"The speculators have done some profit taking, but they are still overextended," said Rich Wistisen, vice president of analysis at Commodity Information. "If the CFTC show a huge increase in spec longs, it could spark more profit taking."
Volume Friday reached an estimated 11,643 lots.
